descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1897
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897, chosen by its conservative gold-standard wing after two defeats on free silver

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1897
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist, a Prohibition, a People's party and a Socialist Labor nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Roosevelt, Parker, Fairbanks, Davis, Debs, Swallow, Watson, McKinley, Bryan, Cleveland or Hearst

slice_sources.men: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1904 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; women 21+ outside the South; women could vote for president only in Wyoming, Colorado (1893), Utah and Idaho (1896).
slice_sources.south-white: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1904 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement was near complete across the region (Alabama 1901, Virginia 1902 and Texas's 1902 poll tax had joined Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana and North Carolina); the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1904; foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
